backlog.spec: Append the 42 MQN (molecular quantum numbers) counts from rdMolDescriptors.MQNs_(mol) to each molecule's feature vector, next to the existing Morgan bits and full descList columns. Apply the same 1st/99th-percentile clipping that the script already uses for descriptors, fitted on the training fold only. Nothing else changes. MQN is not part of Descriptors.descList, so this adds integer count information the current feature set lacks.
backlog.title: MQN count descriptor block

backlog.spec: Add a kernel member that works on continuous descriptors instead of fingerprints. Fit a QuantileTransformer (normal output) on the training-fold clipped full descriptor matrix, then fit sklearn SVC(kernel='rbf', C=1.0, gamma='scale', probability=True, random_state=seed) on it. Use its test probabilities as the replacement for the LightGBM member's score in the rank blend, so the blend stays two-member RF plus SVC. Standardize with the training-fold statistics only.
backlog.title: RBF-SVC member on quantile-scaled descriptors

backlog.spec: Keep the RF and LightGBM members unchanged. Change the final blend from equal weights to 0.6 * scaled_rank(RF) + 0.4 * scaled_rank(LightGBM), then rescale the result to [0, 1] with scaled_rank again so the output stays a rank score. Pick the 0.6/0.4 split from a fixed prior, not by tuning on the reported folds. This is a single-line change in fit_predict.
backlog.title: Asymmetric rank-blend weights

backlog.spec: Keep the 300-tree forest on the existing features and set min_samples_leaf=3 and max_depth=18 in RandomForestClassifier. The aim is smoother class-1 probabilities that rank better across unseen scaffolds, and this is a regularization test on forest complexity. Leave the LightGBM member and the rank blend unchanged, so the only change is the forest constructor arguments.
backlog.title: Shallower-leaf RF with a depth cap

backlog.spec: Raise the RandomForestClassifier to n_estimators=1000 and switch max_features from 0.3 to 'sqrt', keeping min_samples_leaf=1 and random_state=seed. More trees reduce the variance of the forest's rank scores, and sqrt feature sampling decorrelates trees on the wide full-descriptor matrix. Runtime should stay well under the 10-minute job limit because the features and LightGBM member are unchanged.
backlog.title: Larger forest with sqrt feature sampling

backlog.spec: Replace the LightGBM member's default binary log-loss with a custom objective that is a noise-robust symmetric cross-entropy: alpha*CE + beta*RCE, with alpha=1.0, beta=0.5 and the reverse term clipped log(1e-4) for log(0). Pass it to lgb.train as the objective, with the gradient and Hessian derived analytically from the sigmoid of the raw score, and keep 300 rounds at learning_rate 0.05. The rest of the pipeline stays the same. The objective down-weights confidently wrong labels, which the blood-brain barrier labels may contain.
backlog.title: Symmetric cross-entropy LightGBM objective

backlog.spec: Replace the LightGBM member with sklearn AdaBoostClassifier(estimator=DecisionTreeClassifier(max_depth=2), n_estimators=300, learning_rate=0.1, random_state=seed) fitted on the same training matrix. Use its predict_proba class-1 column as the second rank-blend member, with the RF member unchanged. This tests a different boosting mechanism, exponential-loss reweighting with shallow trees, against the current gradient-boosted member.
backlog.title: AdaBoost depth-2 trees instead of LightGBM

backlog.spec: Compute out-of-fold RF scores on the training fold with a 3-fold split, using the same seed. The residual for each training molecule is its label minus its OOF score. For each test molecule, find its 10 nearest training molecules by Tanimoto similarity on the Morgan bits and add the similarity-weighted mean residual, scaled by 0.5, to its blended score before the final rank step. This pushes predictions toward the local label pattern the global model misses.
backlog.title: Residual correction from training neighbours

backlog.spec: Keep the LightGBM member, but at rounds 100, 200 and 300 of a manual training loop with lgb.train, compute per-row log-loss on the training fold and drop the 5% of rows with the largest loss from the next block of rounds. Each block reuses the previous model through init_model. Use the trimmed training matrix only, so the test predictions come from the final model. This is an in-boosting noise filter, a different mechanism from the one-shot denoising and filtering ideas already tried.
backlog.title: Loss-based row trimming inside LightGBM

backlog.spec: Keep the LightGBM member's architecture but change its schedule. Use a 500-round lgb.train booster with learning_rate decaying linearly from 0.1 to 0.01 across rounds, through a callback that resets the learning_rate parameter each round, and keep num_leaves=15 and colsample_bytree=0.3. The forest and blend stay unchanged. The change tests whether a smaller late-stage step improves ranking across unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Learning-rate decay for the LightGBM member

backlog.spec: Keep the LightGBM member but pass interaction_constraints so that splits may only combine features within the same family. Define four groups over the feature matrix: the 11 physchem columns plus the full descList block (size and polarity), the 167 MACCS-free Morgan bits (fingerprint), and the 2048-bit Morgan block split off from the descriptors. Build the constraint list as lists of column indices, one per group, and leave the rest of the model unchanged (300 rounds, lr 0.05, num_leaves 15, colsample 0.3, seed from the argument). This limits spurious cross-family interactions in a 1.6k-row dataset without adding any new features.
backlog.title: Interaction-constrained LightGBM over descriptor families

backlog.spec: Before fitting the RF and LightGBM, compute one supervised feature: a Fisher linear discriminant direction on the clipped full-descriptor matrix, standardized and with shrinkage covariance (Ledoit-Wolf or covariance + 0.1*I). To avoid leakage, produce the training-row values out-of-fold with an inner 5-fold stratified split on the training fold (each row scored by a discriminant fit without it), and produce test-row values from a discriminant fit on the full training fold. Append the single scalar projection as one extra column to both matrices. The idea is a linear, class-aware summary that trees can split on directly.
backlog.title: Out-of-fold Fisher LDA projection feature

backlog.spec: Append a small vector of raw element counts per molecule: counts of F, Cl, Br, I, P, S, B, Si and Se, total halogen count, and heteroatom fraction (non-C, non-H heavy atoms divided by heavy atoms). Compute them in descriptors() with plain RDKit atom loops, store them as float32 columns, and append them after the existing 11 physchem columns, before the full descList block. Clip them with the same 1st/99th percentile rule used for the descriptors. This is a deliberately small, interpretable addition aimed at halogen and sulfur effects on membrane permeation.
backlog.title: Element and heteroatom count block

backlog.spec: Fit the existing RandomForest on the training fold as now. Use rf.apply(X) to get the leaf index of every training and test row in every tree. One-hot encode the leaf indices with sklearn OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore') fitted on the training leaves, giving a very sparse binary matrix with one active column per tree. Train a LogisticRegression (C=0.05, max_iter=2000, seeded) on that embedding and use its test probability as a third signal in place of the LightGBM member, so the blend becomes RF rank plus embedding-logistic rank. This is a bolder change that turns the forest into a learned sparse representation and lets a linear model reweight which tree leaves matter.
backlog.title: Random-forest leaf embedding with a regularized logistic head

backlog.spec: Replace the RandomForest member with a sparse linear model. Build the input from the binary 2048-bit Morgan vector plus the standardized clipped full descriptor matrix (z-score using training-fold mean and std, with zero-variance columns dropped). Fit LogisticRegression(penalty='l1', solver='liblinear', C=0.1, max_iter=2000, random_state=seed) and keep the LightGBM member and the rank blend exactly as they are. This tests whether a linear, sparsity-driven model on the same inputs generalises better across unseen scaffolds than the forest. It is a bold model-family swap, so the blend weights should stay equal.
backlog.title: L1 logistic regression on Morgan bits and descriptors replaces the forest

backlog.spec: Train a pairwise ranker that targets AUROC directly. Sample about 150k random pairs (i, j) from the training fold with y_i != y_j, using a seed-driven generator. For each pair, build the feature x_i - x_j on the clipped, standardized full-descriptor matrix and label it 1 if y_i = 1 and y_j = 0, otherwise 0 (with random sign flipping to keep the label balanced). Fit a LogisticRegression without intercept (C=1.0) or a LightGBM with 200 rounds on these difference rows. For a test molecule, the score is the mean over a fixed set of 200 training anchors of the predicted pairwise probability of its difference against each anchor, mapped to a rank. Use this rank as an extra member in the existing blend, or use it alone to compare. The design rewards correct ordering rather than calibrated probabilities.
backlog.title: Pairwise difference ranker on descriptors

backlog.spec: Replace the binary logloss of the LightGBM member with a squared-hinge margin loss implemented as a custom objective passed to lgb.train. Map labels to s = 2y - 1, let margin m = s * raw_score, and use gradient g = -2 * s * max(0, 1 - m) and hessian h = 2 * 1[m < 1] + 1e-3 (a small floor keeps the leaves stable). Keep 300 rounds, lr 0.05, num_leaves 15, colsample_bytree 0.3, and convert the raw score to a rank for the blend with a sigmoid-free ordering (rank of raw score). Everything else, including the RandomForest member and the rank blend, stays unchanged.
backlog.title: Squared-hinge custom objective for the LightGBM member

backlog.spec: Add annealed noise to the LightGBM member's training signal so that early trees explore and late trees settle. Use a custom objective that returns the usual logloss gradient and hessian plus Gaussian noise on the gradient, with standard deviation 0.3 * (1 - t/T) where t is the round index and T = 300, drawn from a numpy Generator seeded from the seed argument. Keep the hessian unchanged. Leave the rest of the LightGBM settings and the RF member as they are. The noise schedule is the only new element, so any gain or loss can be attributed to the annealing.
backlog.title: Decaying gradient-noise injection during boosting

backlog.spec: Before fitting, cluster training molecules by Morgan Tanimoto similarity with a simple greedy pass: sort rows by index, and assign a molecule to an existing cluster if its Tanimoto to the cluster seed is at least 0.9. Replace each cluster with one representative row whose label is the cluster-mean label, and use sample_weight equal to cluster size for the RF and LightGBM fits. Keep the test-time featurization unchanged. This removes near-duplicate analogue series that dominate the forest's bootstrap and tests whether down-weighting redundant analogues helps generalisation to new scaffolds.
backlog.title: Near-duplicate collapse of training molecules before fitting

backlog.spec: Keep the RandomForest training as now, but after fitting, prune each tree so that any internal node whose subtree holds fewer than 8 training samples is collapsed into a leaf whose value is the node's class probability. Implement this on the fitted sklearn tree arrays (children_left, children_right, value) before prediction, or equivalently refit trees with min_samples_leaf=8 only on the splits that retain support. Then predict as before. The aim is smoother probability estimates on rare fingerprint and descriptor regions, a regularizer that is distinct from raising min_samples_leaf uniformly, which was already tested.
backlog.title: Post-pruning of forest leaves below a minimum support

backlog.spec: In featurize, after the Morgan bits and before the descriptor columns, append the RDKit ErG reduced-graph pharmacophore fingerprint from rdkit.Chem.rdReducedGraphs.GetErGFingerprint(mol) (a float vector of about 315 values, computed per molecule). Keep the rest of fit_predict unchanged (same RF and LightGBM blend, same full-descriptor clipping). Because ErG encodes pharmacophore-pair distances over reduced graphs, it is a different view of the molecule from Morgan bits. Wrap the call in try/except and fall back to zeros on failure so no fold crashes.
backlog.title: ErG pharmacophore reduced-graph fingerprint

backlog.spec: Add two dense blocks per molecule, computed with rdkit.Chem.EState.Fingerprinter.FingerprintMol(mol): the 79-bin EState-count fingerprint (fp[0]) and the 79-value EState index vector (fp[1]). Concatenate them to the feature matrix after the existing descriptors, then apply the same train-fold 1st/99th percentile clipping used for the descriptors. Leave the model settings unchanged. EState indices encode electronic and topological environment of each atom type, which Morgan bits do not capture well.
backlog.title: EState fingerprint and EState index block

backlog.spec: Compute Gasteiger partial charges with rdkit.Chem.rdPartialCharges.ComputeGasteigerCharges(mol) once per molecule. From the per-atom charges, build 8 numbers: max and min charge over all atoms, sum of absolute charges, and for heteroatoms (N or O) the max, min, mean and count of charges, plus the count of atoms with |charge| > 0.2. Replace NaN and inf with 0, clip to the train-fold 1st/99th percentiles, and append to the feature matrix. Model and blend stay the same. This adds an electrostatic view of polarity that the existing TPSA and HBD/HBA counts only approximate.
backlog.title: Gasteiger partial-charge statistics on polar atoms

backlog.spec: Using rdkit.Chem.Crippen._GetAtomContribs or the atom typing in Crippen (per-atom Crippen type labels), count how many atoms of each of the roughly 110 Crippen types each molecule contains, producing a dense integer vector. Append it to the feature matrix after the descriptors and clip with the train-fold percentiles. This gives a full atom-environment composition profile at a coarser level than Morgan bits. Keep RF and LightGBM settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Crippen atom-type count vector

backlog.spec: Replace the global blend for a bold test: for every test molecule, select its k=150 nearest training molecules in the standardized clipped full-descriptor space (Euclidean, using the training-fold scaler). Fit an L2 logistic regression (C=0.3, max_iter=500, seeded) on just those 150 rows with the 11 physchem columns plus the full descriptor columns that have nonzero variance in that neighbourhood, and use its probability for that test molecule. Average this local score with the existing rank blend 50/50. Local models adapt to the chemical region each test point lies in, which a single global forest cannot do. Cache the scaler per fold so the local fits stay fast enough for 15 fits within 10 minutes.
backlog.title: Local logistic model around each test molecule

backlog.spec: Instead of always averaging RF and LightGBM, use training-set density to route each test molecule. For each test molecule compute its mean distance to its 10 nearest training molecules in the standardized clipped descriptor space, and compare it against the 90th percentile of the same statistic computed for training molecules via their own 10 nearest neighbours excluding themselves. Molecules inside the training density use the existing rank blend. Molecules outside it use the RF score alone, because the boosted model extrapolates poorly there. Blend with a rank-preserving mapping so the overall ranking stays on one scale.
backlog.title: Density-gated model selection

backlog.spec: In the LightGBM member, set feature_fraction=1.0 and feature_fraction_bynode=0.2 (replacing colsample_bytree=0.3), keeping num_leaves=15, learning_rate=0.05 and 300 estimators. Node-level sampling decorrelates splits within a tree rather than across the whole tree, which is a different regularizer from the per-tree column sample already used. Keep the RF and the rank blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Node-level feature subsampling in LightGBM

backlog.spec: Train the LightGBM member once for 300 rounds as now. Instead of using only the final model, predict with the booster at num_iteration = 150, 200, 250 and 300, convert each to a rank score on the test set, and average those four rank scores as the LightGBM component. This gives a cheap Polyak-style average over late boosting states with no extra fitting cost. Keep the RF and the rank blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Averaged LightGBM checkpoints

backlog.spec: Replace the single RF member with an ensemble of 8 random Gaussian projections. For each projection j (seeded by seed + j), draw a random matrix of shape (number of standardized clipped full descriptors, 64) from N(0, 1/sqrt(64)) and project the standardized clipped descriptors onto it. Fit one ExtraTreesClassifier (150 trees, max_features=0.3, seeded) on the projected features concatenated with the 2048 Morgan bits. Average the 8 probability vectors and rank-average that with the LightGBM member. This is a random-subspace and rotation view, not a bagging over rows.
backlog.title: Random-projection ExtraTrees ensemble

backlog.spec: Before fitting the LightGBM member, sample 80% of the training scaffolds (Murcko, generic-form not required) per boosting replicate and train 5 LightGBMs of 300 trees each on those row subsets, using bagging_fraction=1.0 within each replicate. Average the 5 rank scores as the LightGBM component. This differs from earlier scaffold-bootstrap bagging in that the subsets are drawn without replacement, so no duplicated rows appear. Keep the RF member and the rank blend unchanged.
